config.title: currentColor and opacity

intro.title: currentColor and opacity
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple card component with a header and body to learn how to use the `currentColor` keyword and `opacity` property in CSS. You will understand that `currentColor` acts as a dynamic variable that inherits the current text color, allowing for consistent theming, while `opacity` controls the transparency of an element and its children. The main technologies involved are CSS properties for color, borders, and transparency. By the end, you will apply these concepts to style the card's border and background with inherited colors and adjust visibility with opacity, reinforcing how CSS values cascade and interact.
intro.usecase: The currentColor and opacity properties are essential for creating cohesive, maintainable design systems in real-world applications. In dashboard interfaces, currentColor ensures icons and decorative elements automatically match text colors when themes change, while opacity creates subtle hover states on data cards and faded disabled form controls. Product teams use these properties in navigation menus to indicate active states with semi-transparent overlays and in modals to dim background content without hard-coded colors. This approach allows developers to build consistent, theme-aware UIs with minimal CSS maintenance.

objectives: Apply the currentColor keyword to inherit color values across CSS properties.
Configure opacity to control the transparency of HTML elements.
Integrate currentColor with border and box-shadow properties for consistent theming.
Manipulate background and text color opacity using RGBA and HSLA color models.
Construct layered visual effects by combining opacity with pseudo-elements.
Update element states (like :hover) using currentColor for dynamic styling.
Render semi-transparent overlays by adjusting opacity on positioned elements.

steps.title: Create a CSS rule for a container element
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule that targets a class named .container. Set its width to 100%, margin to 0 auto, and padding to 20px.
steps.hint: Start with .container { } and add the three properties inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .container is created with width, margin, and padding properties.
successCriteria: The .container rule exists with width: 100%, margin: 0 auto, and padding: 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .container rule includes all three properties: width, margin, and padding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule is missing or incomplete. Create a .container rule with width: 100%, margin: 0 auto, and padding: 20px.

steps.title: Add a box element inside the container
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a .box element that will be nested inside the .container element.
steps.hint: Define a new CSS rule starting with .box { } to style the box element.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your .container rule here */

/* Add your .box rule here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A .box CSS rule is created, ready to be styled with currentColor and opacity properties in later steps.
successCriteria: The code contains a .box CSS rule definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a CSS rule for .box with opening and closing braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a CSS rule for .box. It should look like: .box { }

steps.title: Set a color on the container element
steps.instruction: Add a color property to the .container rule to establish a base color value (e.g., color: #3498db;).
steps.hint: Use the color property inside the .container rule to set a color value like a hex code, named color, or RGB value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will have a color property with a valid color value, establishing a base color that can be inherited.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains a color property with a valid color value (e.g., hex, named color, RGB).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a color property inside the .container rule with a valid color value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container rule should contain a color property with a valid color value (e.g., color: #3498db;).

steps.title: Apply currentColor to the box's border
steps.instruction: In the .box rule, add a border property with a width of 2px, solid style, and use currentColor for the border color.
steps.hint: The currentColor keyword will automatically inherit the color value from the parent container. Use the border shorthand property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a 2px solid border that inherits its color from the .container's color property.
successCriteria: The .box rule contains a border property with width, style, and currentColor for the border-color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure to include all three parts: width (2px), style (solid), and currentColor for the border color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box rule doesn't have the correct border property. Remember to use the border shorthand with currentColor.

steps.title: Apply currentColor to the box's text color
steps.instruction: Inside the .box rule, set the color property to currentColor to inherit the container's text color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule will have a color property set to currentColor, allowing it to inherit the text color from its parent container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'color: currentColor;' inside the .box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box rule should include 'color: currentColor;' to inherit the container's text color.

steps.title: Add a background color to the box
steps.instruction: In the .box rule, add a background-color property with a dark color value (like #2c3e50) to create visual contrast for the upcoming opacity demonstration.
steps.hint: Add a background-color property inside the .box rule. Choose a dark color that will contrast well with the text and border colors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule will have a background-color property with a dark color value.
successCriteria: The .box rule contains a background-color property with a valid color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a background-color property with a valid color value inside the .box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box rule doesn't contain a background-color property with a valid color value. Add background-color: #2c3e50; or another dark color inside the .box rule.

steps.title: Apply opacity to the box element
steps.instruction: Add an opacity property to the .box rule to make it semi-transparent.
steps.hint: Use the opacity property with a value between 0 and 1. For example, opacity: 0.7; will make the box 70% opaque.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule will include an opacity property, making the box element semi-transparent.
successCriteria: The .box CSS rule contains an opacity property with a valid value (e.g., 0.7).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the opacity property is correctly added to the .box rule with a value like 0.7.
steps.feedbackWrong: The opacity property is missing or incorrect in the .box rule. Try adding opacity: 0.7; inside the .box {}.

steps.title: Add text content styling to the box
steps.instruction: Add padding and font-size properties to the .box rule to create visible text content.
steps.hint: Add padding to create space inside the box and font-size to make the text readable. For example, you could use padding: 1rem; and font-size: 1.2rem;
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule will have padding and font-size properties, making text content more visible and readable.
successCriteria: The .box rule contains padding and font-size properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both padding and font-size properties to the .box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box rule should include padding and font-size properties to style the text content.

steps.title: Create a second box with different opacity
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a second box element with class name '.box2' and set its opacity to 0.3.
steps.hint: Add a new selector for .box2 and include the opacity property with a value of 0.3.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second box element with class 'box2' is defined with opacity set to 0.3, allowing comparison with the first box's opacity.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a .box2 selector with opacity: 0.3; property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .box2 rule, but make sure to include the opacity property with a value of 0.3.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a new CSS rule for .box2 with opacity set to 0.3. Please add the .box2 selector and opacity property.

steps.title: Add hover effect using opacity
steps.instruction: Add a hover pseudo-class to the .box element that changes its opacity to 1 when hovered.
steps.hint: Use the selector .box:hover and set opacity: 1; inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will become fully opaque when the mouse hovers over it.
successCriteria: A .box:hover selector is added with opacity: 1;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct selector .box:hover and setting opacity to 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using .box:hover with opacity: 1;
